brief: A Market Ear note (citing Goldman's trading desk, Prime, GIR and Marquee research) argues the 'boring' quality factor is resurging as momentum and AI-linked trades lose steam. Goldman's sector/industry/factor-neutral Quality Pair Index (GSP1QUAL) is up 5% in five days and 20% over three months to a 12-month high on about 13% realized volatility. Market leadership is shifting from growth-at-any-price to quality of earnings, a rotation the note expects to be reinforced as earnings growth decelerates across both AI and non-AI sectors over the next 12 months, with higher rates being priced in adding a further tailwind. Quality now shows a strong negative correlation to AI, momentum and high-beta exposure, acting as a hedge against those crowded trades, and the note argues quality historically outperforms once earnings revisions roll over. Momentum and beta positioning are elevated (78th and 81st percentile over five years respectively), leaving room for a painful unwind. The long-quality/short-momentum trade is already up 55% in 2026, which the note frames as the possible start of a structural rotation.
